title: One set of easing curves, named the same way everywhere
goal: Four different lists of easing options are on screen across the mock pages right now, so the same control offers you Spring on one screen and not on the next, with no reason a person could see. Settle one short list of named curves and make every page that lets you shape a motion offer that list, so the icon motion work about to be built starts from one vocabulary instead of inheriting four.
notes:
Found while comparing the animation and video flows (task say-where-animating-an-icon-and-editing-a-video). Reproduced, not read:

  $ cd docs/design/mocks
  $ for f in pages/icon-animate-wt.html pages/icon-loop-wt.html pages/icon-states-wt.html pages/icon-drawon-wt.html pages/video-move-wt.html pages/video-zoom-wt.html; do echo "--- $f"; grep -A6 'aria-label="Easing"' $f | grep -o '>[A-Za-z ][A-Za-z -]*</button>' | sed 's/>//;s;</button>;;'; done

  --- pages/icon-loop-wt.html

  --- pages/video-move-wt.html

The design language already has exactly three curves and names them in tokens.css: --ease-standard cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), --ease-decel cubic-bezier(0,0,.2,1), --ease-spring cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.5,1), documented on pages/lang-motion.html. None of the six user-facing controls above maps cleanly onto those three names. Deciding the mapping (which label means --ease-decel: "Ease out"?) is the substance of the task.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: easing is one of only three things the animation and video flows genuinely share (see docs/design/animation-vs-video.md and the time-compare page). It is the cheapest consolidation on offer and it has already drifted in mocks alone, before a line of app code exists.
acceptance: One named set of curves is written down in the shared motion rules, with the design tokens each name maps to
Every mock page with an Easing control offers that same set, in the same order
A check script or the page checklist catches a page that invents its own set, so this cannot drift again silently
The video pages offer the same curve control as the icon pages, not their own list
The curve control is defined once rather than pasted into each page that needs it

log.note: Partly done, on the icon side only. 2026-09-15 the property-first animation mocks landed ONE curve control and it is now on all five icon pages (icon-animate-wt, icon-phase-wt, icon-loop-wt, icon-states-wt, icon-drawon-wt): a select opening a menu of named curves with each curve's SHAPE drawn beside its name (Linear, the four standard eases, ease in out sine, ease out back, ease out elastic, steps 4) plus 'Draw a curve...' opening a cubic-bezier editor with two draggable handles and the cubic-bezier(a,b,c,d) readout. The three-button segmented easing control is gone from every icon page. What is LEFT for this task is the video side: the video pages still carry their own easing vocabularies, and the curve menu markup is duplicated per page rather than living in shared/components, so a sixth page would copy it again. Adding to acceptance: the same curve control appears on the video pages too, and it is defined once rather than pasted per page.

The revised animation-vs-video study (docs/design/mocks/pages/time-compare.html, proof three) reproduces both sides at their real markup: the icon pages now carry one curve list with the shape drawn beside each name plus a drawn cubic-bezier, and the video pages still carry a two-button segmented control (Linear / Ease in-out, video-zoom-wt step 7). So the drift is no longer four vocabularies disagreeing, it is one settled vocabulary and a video side that has not adopted it. The remaining work on this task is the video side.

The APP side is now settled, by the motion model that landed today (Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift, EasingCurve). One named list, in one order, with each shape drawn beside its name wherever a curve is offered or shown: Linear, Ease in out, Ease in, Ease out, Ease in out sine, Ease out back, Ease out elastic, Steps 4, and 'Draw a curve...' for a cubic-bezier you drag two handles to make. That is the same list the five icon mock pages carry, so the app and the study agree.

The MAPPING this task asked somebody to settle, now written down in docs/design/layer-motion.md and covered by a test (theNamedEasesAreTheDesignLanguagesOwnTokens):
  Ease in out  = cubic-bezier(.4, 0, .2, 1)  = tokens.css --ease-standard
  Ease out     = cubic-bezier(0, 0, .2, 1)   = tokens.css --ease-decel
  Ease in      = cubic-bezier(.4, 0, 1, 1)   (the accelerate mirror of decel)
  --ease-spring is what Ease out back is doing, under the name people use for it.
Note that Ease in out is therefore NOT symmetrical: --ease-standard is fast out and slow in, so it reads 0.78 at half time. Anyone expecting CSS's own ease-in-out (0.42,0,0.58,1) will find this different, and that was the choice: the design language's token wins over the CSS keyword.

What is still LEFT on this task is unchanged: the video mock pages still carry their own two-button segmented easing control, and the curve menu markup is duplicated per page rather than living in shared/components.

Adversarial review BEFORE building. (1) The video walkthroughs traded a one-click segmented switch for a two-click menu, which is slower for the two curves they name. Built it anyway: the icon side already made that trade on purpose (a segmented group can only offer three curves and the fourth thing anyone wants is not on it), and a video move wanting an overshoot has nowhere to go today. (2) video.html's keyframe card offered six chips including Hold. Hold is NOT a curve, it is the absence of a transition, so folding it into a list of eight shapes would have made the list mean two kinds of thing. It is now a separate flag on the key (k.hold), the curve it suspends is shown faded rather than replaced, and picking a curve lifts the hold. (3) video-speed's Ramp/Hold is how a speed stop joins the next one, not an easing vocabulary: left alone deliberately. (4) video-audio said 'S-curve', a name nowhere else in the study, for what is plainly Ease in out. Converted. (5) Steps, 4 and Ease out elastic on a camera punch-in are odd, but one list beats two lists, and that is the whole task.

SHIPPED. The list is defined once, in docs/design/mocks/shared/components/curve.{css,js} (registered in order.json, css after segmented, js right after core so rows exist before popover.js and walkthrough.js run). A page writes an EMPTY host and the component fills it:

PZ.curve publishes {list, draw, menuHTML, editorHTML, upgrade, thumb, get, at}; at(id,t) is a line-by-line transliteration of PhotonzCore EasingCurve.value(at:), bezier solver included, verified against dense sampling (max error <2e-3 on four control-point sets) and reading 0.7756 at half time for Ease in out, the number docs/design/layer-motion.md documents. Converted: the five icon pages (rows deleted, page-local .cvth/.bez/.bezval/.mnote CSS deleted, .mnote promoted to app-patterns.css), video-move-wt, video-zoom-wt (segmented Linear/Ease in-out -> Curve select + menu, walkthrough steps re-cued to data-pop #curveMenu + data-cue #easInOut, eased state carried into later steps via data-set), video-motion (the invented 'Ease out . soft'), video-audio (Linear/Ease/S-curve -> the list; curveFn now calls PZ.curve.at, so the drawn fade is the real curve), video.html (toolbar default + per-key curve + a real bezPop; smooth()/spring()/in/out all deleted in favour of the shared evaluator). time-compare.html proof three rewritten: it was the page ARGUING the video side had not adopted this, and it had to stop saying so.

The gate: node shared/check-easing.mjs, three rules, all three PROVEN to fire. (1) a page drawing its own .cvth rows, (2) a segmented group whose buttons are two or more easing words, (3) the component's list drifting from Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift's EasingCurve.named, parsed out of the Swift rather than restated. Proof of (1) and (2): ran it against the pre-change video-zoom-wt, video.html and icon-states-wt from git HEAD, 3 failures, exit 1. Proof of (3): renamed Ease out back to Spring in curve.js, it failed with both lists printed, exit 1. --list prints the one list. Documented in shared/AGENTS.md (gates list), UX-PATTERNS.md D17 (the pattern, with the token mapping and why Hold is not in the list), and pages/lang-motion.html, which now draws the eight beside the three interface tokens and reads them out of curve.js rather than retyping them.

Verified in real Chrome (Playwright, 1680x1050, deviceScaleFactor 2): all 11 touched pages return 200 with zero console errors and render the identical nine rows; every walkthrough on the five icon pages and the two video ones steps end to end with no broken data-cue/data-pop/data-activate target; on video.html the toolbar default, the per-key curve, Hold and Draw a curve all work, and the plotted graph path changes shape per curve (704 chars linear, 1164 ease in out, 1187 back, 1162 elastic, 949 steps, 714 held), so the maths is live rather than decorative. Gates green: check-easing, check-reserved, check-a11y-names, check-elevation, check-states, check-selection, check-shortcuts, check-fieldwrap. build-ds.mjs rebuilt. Scripts/test.sh: 7176 tests in 573 suites, passed (no Swift changed, run as the repo rule requires).

left rough, none of it clearing the follow-up bar: (a) the Draw a curve editor's two handles do not drag in ANY mock that has one, including the icon pages this came from, so it is a study-wide limitation rather than something this task broke; (b) the video keyframe card's menu opens over the timeline lane because the card sits low in the panel, readable but covering what you are editing; (c) Ease out elastic's css field is a bezier stand-in, since the real curve is not a bezier and both the app and PZ.curve.at sample it instead, so only a reader of the css string is affected and nothing reads it; (d) pages/video-speed.html keeps its Ramp / Hold control on purpose, it answers a different question. All four are in the audit's rough list where the user can disagree with any of them.

One easing vocabulary, defined once and gated. shared/components/curve.{css,js} owns the eight names, their order, their drawn shapes, their cubic-beziers and an evaluator; every page asks for it with an empty data-curve-menu host. Converted the five icon pages plus the whole video side (video-move-wt, video-zoom-wt, video-motion, video-audio, video.html), rewrote time-compare proof three, wrote the pattern into UX-PATTERNS D17, AGENTS.md and lang-motion. node shared/check-easing.mjs fails a page that draws its own rows, a segmented group that is its own vocabulary, and a list that has drifted from PhotonzCore's EasingCurve: all three proven to fire against real pre-change source. Verified in real Chrome across 11 pages (no console errors, every walkthrough steps end to end, the plotted graph changes shape per curve). All mock gates green, Scripts/test.sh green (7176 tests).
